Any dharma that is unwholesome, or any retribution of an unwholesome dharma—these are called dharmas that are neither caused by what is not abandoned through insight nor by what is not abandoned through cultivation.
What are the phenomena associated with the desire realm (*kāmadhātu-pratisaṃyukta-dharma*)?
If a phenomenon is characterized by the outflow of desire (*kāma-āsrava*) or is tainted (*sāsrava*), it is called a phenomenon associated with the desire realm.
What are the phenomena not associated with the desire realm?

If a phenomenon belongs to the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) or the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*), or is not bound to any realm, it is called a phenomenon that is not bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).
What is meant by a phenomenon bound to the realm of form?
If a phenomenon is associated with the outflow of form (*rūpāsrava*) and is subject to outflows (*sāsrava*), it is called a phenomenon bound to the realm of form.
What are the factors not bound to the form realm (*ārūpyadhātu*)?
Those that are bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), bound to the formless realm, or are unbound—these are called factors not bound to the form realm.
What are the factors bound to the formless realm?
If a phenomenon is formless, outflowing, and subject to outflows, it is called a phenomenon bound to the formless realm.
What is meant by a phenomenon not bound to the formless realm?
If a phenomenon belongs to the desire realm, the form realm, or is unconditioned (unbound), it is called a phenomenon not bound to the formless realm.
What are the unconditioned (aniyata) dharmas?
Those that are noble, untainted, and unconditioned are called unconditioned dharmas.
What are the non-unconditioned dharmas?
If they are bound to the three realms, these are called non-unbound dharmas.
What are past dharmas? If a dharma has arisen and then ceased, it is called a past dharma.
What is meant by non-past phenomena?
Those that are future or present, or those that are neither past, nor future, nor present—these are called non-past phenomena.
What is meant by future phenomena?
If a phenomenon has not yet arisen and has not yet emerged, it is called a future phenomenon.
What is meant by non-future phenomena?
If it is past or present, or if it is neither past nor future nor present, this is called a non-future phenomenon (*anāgata-dharma*).
What is meant by a present phenomenon (*pratyutpanna-dharma*)?
If a phenomenon has arisen but not yet ceased, it is called a present phenomenon.
What is meant by a non-present phenomenon?
If a phenomenon is past or future, or neither past nor present, it is called a non-present phenomenon.
What is meant by phenomena that are neither past, nor future, nor present?
If a phenomenon is unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*), it is called a phenomenon that is neither past, nor future, nor present.
What is meant by "not non-past, future, and present phenomena"?
If a phenomenon is past, future, or present, this is called "not non-past, future, and present phenomena. This concludes the section on the Dharma-gate of Nature.
Regarding the phenomena associated with the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya-saṃprayukta-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about? They are the phenomena associated with the Truth of Suffering.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding those dharmas bound to the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya*).
Regarding the factors not bound to the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors not bound to the Truth of Suffering.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded? Dharmas bound to the truth of suffering (duḥkhasatya) are excluded.
Regarding the factors associated with the truth of origination (*samudaya-satya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about? They are the factors associated with the truth of origination.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas not bound by the Truth of Origination (samudayasatya) are excluded.
Regarding the factors not bound by the Truth of Origination (*samudaya-satya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors not bound by the Truth of Origination.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded? Dharmas bound to the truth of origination (samudayasatya) are excluded.
Regarding the factors associated with the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya-saṃprayukta-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about? They are the factors associated with the truth of cessation.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding those dharmas bound to the Truth of Cessation (nirodha-satya).
Regarding the factors not bound by the Truth of Cessation (*nirodhasatya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors not bound by the Truth of Cessation.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded? Dharmas associated with the truth of cessation (nirodhasatya) are excluded.
Regarding the factors associated with the Truth of the Path (*mārgasatya-saṃprayukta-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about? They are the factors associated with the Truth of the Path.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding those dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path (mārga-satya).
Regarding the factors not bound by the Truth of the Path (*mārgasatya-saṃprayukta-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors not bound by the Truth of the Path.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded? Dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path (mārgasatya) are excluded.
Regarding the factors bound to the Noble Truths (*āryasatya-saṃprayukta-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors bound to the Noble Truths.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding those dharmas bound to the Noble Truths.
Regarding the factors not bound by the Noble Truths (*anāryasatyasaṃprayukta-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors not bound by the Noble Truths.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas bound to the Noble Truths are excluded.
Regarding the dharmas that are faculties (*indriya*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) are they subsumed?
What dharmas are being asked about? It is the dharmas that are faculties.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Non-faculty dharmas are excluded.
Regarding non-faculty phenomena (*anindriya-dharma*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) are they subsumed?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
They are the non-faculty phenomena.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
The root-dharmas are excluded.
Regarding the factors associated with the Truth of Suffering that are faculties (*indriya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors associated with the Truth of Suffering that are faculties.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding those root-dharmas bound to the Truth of Suffering, and excluding those non-root-dharmas bound to the Truth of Suffering.

Regarding the factors associated with the faculties that are not bound by the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors associated with the faculties that are not bound by the Truth of Suffering.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding those dharmas bound to the truth of suffering (*duḥkhasatya*), and excluding those dharmas not bound to the truth of suffering that are not faculties (*indriya*).
Regarding the factors associated with the truth of origination (*samudaya-satya*) that are roots (*mūla*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors associated with the truth of origination that are roots.

Regarding the factors associated with the truth of origination (*samudaya-satya*) and those not associated with the truth of origination: how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
Question: Regarding those root-dharmas not bound by the truth of origination,
setting aside other dharmas—
what dharmas are being set aside?
Excluding those factors bound to the truth of origination (*samudaya-satya*) and excluding those factors not bound to the truth of origination that are not faculties (*indriya*).
As for the factors bound to the truth of cessation (*nirodha-satya*) that are faculties, how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
Question: Regarding the factors associated with the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*),
the factors not associated with the truth of cessation,
and those factors that are neither associated with nor dissociated from the truth of cessation— how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: What dharmas? Answer:
Dharmas that are not bound to the faculties associated with the truth of cessation;
all other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas bound to the Truth of Cessation (*nirodhasatya*) are excluded, as are those non-faculty dharmas not bound to the Truth of Cessation.
As for the faculty dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path (*mārgasatya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: What dharmas? Answer: Dharmas associated with the path-truth and bound to the faculties;
excluding all other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?

Excluding those dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path and excluding those dharmas not bound to the Truth of the Path that are not faculties—there are no such dharmas not bound to the Truth of the Path that are not faculties.
As for those dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path that are faculties, how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do they comprise?
Question: What kind of phenomena?
Question: Phenomena that are roots bound by the Truth of the Path (mārgasatya).
Exclude all other phenomena.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas associated with the Truth of the Path that are faculties (*indriya*) are excluded, as well as those dharmas not associated with the Truth of the Path that are not faculties.
Among all dharmas associated with the Noble Truths that are faculties, how many are comprised within the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*)?
Question: What dharmas? Question:
The dharmas associated with the noble truths and bound to the faculties;
excluding all other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas bound to the Noble Truths that are faculties are excluded; those dharmas bound to the Noble Truths that are non-faculties are excluded.
How many aggregates, elements, and bases do the dharmas bound to the Noble Truths that are faculties comprise?
Question: Which phenomena? Answer:
Phenomena not bound to the faculties by means of the Noble Truths;
all other phenomena are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas bound to the Noble Truths that are faculties are excluded; those dharmas not bound to the Noble Truths that are not faculties are excluded.
As for the dharmas bound to the Truth of Suffering that are not faculties, how many aggregates, elements, and bases do they comprise?
Question: What dharmas are being asked about?
Answer: Dharmas bound to the truth of suffering that are not faculties (anindriya);
all other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas not bound by the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya*) are excluded, as are those root-dharmas (*indriya*) bound by the Truth of Suffering.
As for those dharmas that are neither bound by the Truth of Suffering nor are roots, how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: What dharmas are being asked about?
Answer: Dharmas that are not bound to the truth of suffering and are not faculties;
all other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas bound to the truth of suffering (*duḥkhasatya*) are excluded, as are those root-dharmas not bound to the truth of suffering.
As for non-root-dharmas bound to the truth of origination (*samudayasatya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: Which dharmas? Question:
Dharmas associated with the truth of origination that are not faculties.
Exclude all other dharmas.
What dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas bound by the Truth of Origination (*samudaya-satya*) are excluded.
There are no root-dharmas (*indriya-dharma*) that are bound by the Truth of Origination which are excluded.

Regarding those phenomena that are neither bound by the Truth of Origination (*samudaya-satya*) nor are faculties (*indriya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
They are the phenomena that are neither bound by the Truth of Origination nor are faculties.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding those dharmas bound to the truth of origination (*samudayasatya*), and excluding those faculties not bound to the truth of origination.

Regarding the non-faculty phenomena associated with the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya-saṃprayukta-avairāgya-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What phenomena are being asked about?
They are the non-faculty phenomena associated with the truth of cessation.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding those dharmas bound to the truth of cessation (nirodhasatya).
There are no factors associated with the Truth of Cessation that are non-faculties (*anindriya*).
As for those factors associated with the Truth of Cessation that are not non-faculties, how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
Question: Regarding those phenomena not bound by the truth of cessation that are not faculties—
excluding other phenomena—
what phenomena are excluded?
Excluding the factors bound to the truth of cessation and excluding the faculties bound to the truth of cessation:
how many aggregates, elements, and bases do the non-faculty factors bound to the truth of the path comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
If one asks about factors bound to the Truth of the Path that are not faculties:
there are none.
As for factors not bound to the Truth of the Path that are not faculties, how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do they comprise?
Question: What dharmas? Question:
Non-factors bound to the Truth of the Path and non-faculties.
Exclude all other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path (*mārga-satya*) are excluded, as are those root-dharmas not bound to the Truth of the Path.
Among all dharmas bound to the Noble Truths that are not roots (*amūla*), how many are comprised within the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*)?
Question: What dharmas? Question:
Those dharmas bound to the noble truths that are not faculties (*indriya*).
Exclude all other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas bound by the Noble Truths are excluded, as are those root-dharmas bound by the Noble Truths.
As for those dharmas not bound by the Noble Truths and which are not roots, how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do they comprise?
Question: What dharmas? Answer:
Those dharmas that are neither bound to the Noble Truths nor are faculties;
excluding all other dharmas.
What dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas bound by the Noble Truths are excluded; those root-dharmas not bound by the Noble Truths are excluded.
Within the dharma of the eye-base (*cakṣur-āyatana*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) are included?
Question: What dharmas are being asked about?
Answer: The dharma of the eye-base (cakṣur-āyatana).
All other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those that are not the eye-base (cakṣur-āyatana).
By how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) are those dharmas that are not the eye-base subsumed?
Question: What kind of phenomena?
Question: Phenomena that are not the eye-base (*cakṣurāyatana*).
Exclude all other phenomena.
What dharmas are excluded?
The dharma of the eye-base (cakṣur-āyatana) is excluded.
This applies likewise up to the dharma-base (dharma-āyatana).
Regarding the dharma of the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) is it subsumed?
What kind of dharma is being asked about?
It is asking about the dharma of the eye-element.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding those dharmas that are not the eye-element (cakṣurdhātu).
Regarding those dharmas that are not the eye-element (*cakṣurdhātu*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of dharmas are being asked about?
They are the dharmas that are not the eye-element.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
The dharma of the eye-element (cakṣurdhātu) is excluded.
This applies even up to the *dharmadhātu*.
Regarding the *dharma* of the aggregate of form (*rūpaskandha*), by how many aggregates, elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) is it subsumed?
What kind of *dharma* is being asked about?
Question: Regarding the dharma of the aggregate of form (rūpaskandha), other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding the phenomena of the aggregate of form (*rūpaskandha*),
how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do the non-form phenomena comprise?
Which phenomena are being asked about?
Question: Regarding non-material (arūpa) aggregates,
with the exception of other phenomena, what phenomena are excluded?
Excluding the aggregate of form (*rūpaskandha*),
the same applies up to the aggregate of consciousness (*vijñānaskandha*).
Regarding the Dharma of the Noble Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatyadharma*), how many aggregates, elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: What dharma is being asked about?
Answer: The dharma of the Noble Truth of Suffering;
all other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas that are not the Noble Truth of Suffering.
How many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do those dharmas that are not the Noble Truth of Suffering comprise?
Question: Which dharmas?
Question: Dharmas that are not the Noble Truth of Suffering.
Excluding all other dharmas.
What dharmas are excluded?
The dharma of the Noble Truth of Suffering is excluded.
This applies likewise up to the dharma of the Noble Truth of the Path.
Regarding the phenomenon of the eye-faculty (*cakṣur-indriya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they subsume?
What phenomena are being asked about?
They are asking about the phenomena of the eye-faculty.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding those dharmas that are not the eye-faculty (cakṣur-indriya).
Regarding the dharmas that are not the eye-faculty (cakṣur-indriya), how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do they comprise?
What kind of dharmas are being asked about?
They are asking about the dharmas that are not the eye-faculty.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
The dharma of the eye-faculty is excluded.
This applies likewise up to the factors associated with the faculty of having known (*ājñātāvīndriya*).
Regarding the factor of the awakening-factor of mindfulness (*smṛti-saṃbodhyaṅga*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) is it comprised?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
Question: Regarding the factor of enlightenment of mindfulness,
with the exclusion of other factors, what factors are excluded?
Excluding the factors associated with the awakening factor of mindfulness,
how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do the factors not associated with the awakening factor of mindfulness comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
Question: Regarding the factors that are not the awakening factor of mindfulness,
setting aside other factors—
what factors are being set aside?
Excluding the factor of the awakening-factor of mindfulness,
the same applies up to the factor of the awakening-factor of equanimity.
As for the factor of the unwholesome root of greed, how many aggregates, elements, and bases does it comprise?
Question: What dharmas are being asked about?
Answer: The dharmas of the unwholesome root of greed;
all other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Those dharmas that are not the unwholesome root of non-greed are excluded.
By how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) are those dharmas that are not the unwholesome root of non-greed subsumed?
Question: What kind of phenomena?
Question: Phenomena that are not the unwholesome root of greed.
Exclude all other phenomena.
What dharmas are excluded?
The unwholesome root of greed is excluded;
the same applies to hatred and delusion.
Regarding the wholesome root of non-attachment (*alobha*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) is it comprised?
What kind of phenomena (*dharma*) are being asked about?
It is the wholesome root of non-attachment that is being asked about.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding those dharmas that are not the wholesome root of non-attachment.
Regarding the non-greed wholesome root-dharmas, how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do they comprise?
What dharmas are being asked about?
They are asking about the dharmas that are not the non-greed wholesome root.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
The dharma of the wholesome root of non-attachment is excluded.
The same applies to non-hatred and non-delusion.
Regarding the great element of earth, by how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) is it subsumed?
What kind of phenomena (dharma) are being asked about?
Question: Regarding the great element of earth,
with the exception of other dharmas—
what dharmas are excluded?
Excluding the great earth element (*mahāpṛthivīdhātu*),
how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) include that which is not the great earth element?
What phenomena (*dharma*) are being asked about?
Question: Regarding the great dharma that is not earth,
setting aside other dharmas—
what dharmas are being set aside?
Excluding the great element of earth,
the same applies to the great elements of water, fire, and wind.
As for the dharma of the precept against killing, how many aggregates (skandhas), elements (dhātus), and bases (āyatanas) does it comprise?
What dharma is being asked about?
It is the dharma of the precept of non-killing;
other dharmas are excluded.
Which phenomena are excluded?
Those that are not the precept of abstaining from taking life are excluded.
How many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do those that are not the precept of abstaining from taking life comprise?
What dharma is being asked about?
It is not the dharma of the precept against taking life;
it excludes all other dharmas.
What dharmas are excluded?
The dharma of the precept against taking life is excluded;
this applies likewise up to the state of non-negligence regarding not drinking alcohol.
Regarding the category of form-dharmas (*rūpa-dharma*): by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) are they subsumed?
What dharmas are being asked about?
Form-dharmas are being asked about.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Non-material (arūpa) dharmas are excluded.
Regarding non-material phenomena (*arūpadharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
They are asking about non-material phenomena.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding material (rūpa) dharmas.
This applies likewise to phenomena of the past, future, and present; thus concludes the section on single categories.
*Śāriputra-abhidharma-śāstra*, Fascicle Twenty-one.
*Śāriputra-abhidharma-śāstra*, Fascicle Twenty-two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmayaśas of Kaśmīra, together with Dharmagupta and others, during the Yao Qin dynasty.
Section on Compendium, Chapter One, Part Two:
Regarding the factors associated with the Truth of Suffering within the aggregate of form (*rūpa*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: What dharmas? Answer: The dharmas of the truth of suffering associated with form;
excluding all other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Non-material dharmas are excluded, as well as material dharmas that are not bound to the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya*).
How many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) include those material dharmas that are not bound to the Truth of Suffering?
Question: What kind of phenomena?
Answer: Phenomena that are matter (rūpa) and not bound to the Truth of Suffering;
all other phenomena are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Non-material dharmas are excluded, as are material dharmas bound to the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya*).
How many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do material dharmas bound to the Truth of Origination (*samudayasatya*) comprise?
Question: What kind of phenomena?
Question: Phenomena associated with the truth of the origin of form (*rūpa-samudaya-satya-saṃprayukta-dharma*). Answer: None.
Regarding the question: "How many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) subsume that which is form (rūpa) not bound by the Truth of Origination (samudaya-satya)?
What dharma is being asked about?
It is asking about form not bound by the Truth of Origination.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Non-material (arūpa) dharmas are excluded.
Excluding those phenomena bound by the Truth of Origination within the aggregate of form, there are none.
Regarding those phenomena bound by the Truth of Cessation within the aggregate of form: how many aggregates, elements, and bases do they comprise?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
Question: Regarding the phenomena associated with the truth of cessation (nirodha-satya) within the aggregate of form (rūpa), there are none.
As for those phenomena of form that are not associated with the truth of cessation, how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do they comprise?
Question: Which dharmas? Answer:
Form (rūpa) that is not bound by the Truth of Cessation (nirodha-satya).
All other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Non-material (arūpa) dharmas are excluded.
There are no material dharmas bound to the truth of cessation (nirodhasatya-saṃyukta) that are excluded.
Regarding the factors associated with the Truth of the Path within the aggregate of form (*rūpa-skandha*), how many aggregates, elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors associated with the Truth of the Path within the aggregate of form.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-material dharmas and excluding material dharmas that are not bound by the Truth of the Path.
Regarding the question: "How many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) subsume those phenomena that are matter (rūpa) and not bound by the Truth of the Path (mārgasatya)?
What phenomena are being asked about?
It is asking about those phenomena that are matter and not bound by the Truth of the Path.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-material dharmas and excluding those dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path that are material.
Regarding the phenomena associated with the Noble Truths of Form (*rūpa*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What phenomena are being asked about?
They are the phenomena associated with the Noble Truths of Form.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-material dharmas, and excluding material dharmas that are not bound by the Noble Truths.
Regarding the question of how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) subsume that which is form (rūpa) not bound by the Noble Truths—
what kind of phenomena are being asked about?
It is asking about form that is not bound by the Noble Truths.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-material dharmas and excluding those material dharmas bound to the Noble Truths.
Regarding the category of material faculties (*rūpindriya-dharma*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) are they subsumed?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
They are asking about the category of material faculties.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-material dharmas and excluding material dharmas that are not faculties.
Regarding the non-faculty dharmas of form (*rūpa*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) are they subsumed?
What dharmas are being asked about?
It is the non-faculty dharmas of form that are being asked about.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Non-material dharmas are excluded, and material faculties are excluded.

Regarding the factors associated with the truth of suffering that are of the nature of the faculties (*indriya*) within the aggregate of form (*rūpa-skandha*): by how many aggregates, elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) are they subsumed?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors associated with the truth of suffering that are of the nature of the faculties within the aggregate of form.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?

Excluding non-material dharmas; excluding material dharmas that are not bound by the Truth of Suffering; excluding material dharmas that are bound by the Truth of Suffering but are not faculties (*indriya*).

Regarding the dharmas that are form (*rūpa*), not bound by the truth of suffering (*duḥkhasatya*), and are faculties (*indriya*): how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What dharmas are being asked about?
They are the dharmas that are form, not bound by the truth of suffering, and are faculties.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?

Excluding non-material dharmas; excluding material dharmas bound to the Truth of Suffering; excluding material dharmas that are neither bound to the Truth of Suffering nor faculties—there are none [to exclude].

Regarding the factors associated with the truth of the origin of form that are root-factors (*indriya-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of factors are being asked about?
They are the factors associated with the truth of the origin of form that are root-factors.
There are none.

As for the question: "How many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) include those phenomena that are not bound by the truth of origination (samudaya-satya) and are not root-phenomena (mūla-dharma)?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
Question: Regarding the factors that are not the roots associated with the truth of origination (*samudaya-satya*) among the factors of form (*rūpa*),
excluding other factors—
what factors are excluded?

Excluding matter-dharmas, excluding those matter-dharmas bound to the truth of the origin (*samudaya-satya*), and excluding those matter-dharmas that are neither bound to the truth of the origin nor are faculties (*indriya*),
how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do those matter-dharmas bound to the truth of cessation (*nirodha-satya*) that are faculties comprise?
Question: What kind of phenomena?
Answer: Phenomena that are bound to the faculty of the truth of the cessation of form (*rūpa-nirodha-satya*).
None exist.

Regarding the question: "How many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) include matter (rūpa) that is not bound by the truth of cessation (nirodhasatya) and is a faculty-dharma (indriyadharma)?
What dharma is being asked about?
It is asking about matter that is not bound by the truth of cessation and is a faculty-dharma.
Excluding other dharmas. Which dharmas are excluded? Excluding non-material (arūpa) dharmas;

excluding material dharmas bound to the truth of cessation (nirodhasatya), which do not exist; and excluding material dharmas that are neither bound to the truth of cessation nor are faculties (indriya).

Regarding the dharmas that are roots associated with the truth of the path within the aggregate of form (*rūpa-skandha*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What dharmas are being asked about?
They are the dharmas that are roots associated with the truth of the path within the aggregate of form.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-material dharmas; excluding material dharmas that are not bound to the Truth of the Path; there are no material dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path that are not faculties.

Regarding the question: "How many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) include matter (rūpa) that is not bound by the Truth of the Path (mārgasatya) and is a faculty-dharma (indriyadharma)?
What dharma is being asked about?
It is asking about matter that is not bound by the Truth of the Path and is a faculty-dharma.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-material dharmas, and excluding those material dharmas that are not bound by the Truth of the Path and are not faculties.

Regarding the phenomena of the form aggregate that are bound by the noble truths and associated with the faculties (*indriya*), how many aggregates, elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What phenomena are being asked about?
They are the phenomena of the form aggregate that are bound by the noble truths and associated with the faculties.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-material dharmas; excluding material dharmas that are not bound by the Noble Truths; excluding material dharmas that are neither bound by the Noble Truths nor are faculties.
Regarding the question: "How many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) include the matter that is not bound by the noble truths and is not a faculty-based dharma?
What dharma is being asked about?
It is asking about the matter that is not bound by the noble truths and is not a faculty-based dharma.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-material dharmas; excluding material dharmas bound to the Noble Truths; there are no material dharmas that are neither bound to the Noble Truths nor are faculties.

Regarding the non-faculty dharmas associated with the truth of suffering within the aggregate of form (*rūpa-skandha*), how many aggregates, elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What dharmas are being asked about?
They are the non-faculty dharmas associated with the truth of suffering within the aggregate of form.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-material dharmas, excluding material dharmas not bound to the Truth of Suffering, and excluding material dharmas bound to the Truth of Suffering that are faculties.

Regarding the matter of form (*rūpa*) that is neither bound by the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya*) nor a faculty (*indriya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What dharma is being asked about?
It is the dharma of form that is neither bound by the Truth of Suffering nor a faculty.
There are none.

As for the non-faculty phenomena associated with the truth of the origin of form (*rūpa-samudaya-satya-saṃprayukta-ahetuka-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
Question: Regarding matter that is bound by the truth of origination and is not a faculty (*indriya*), there are none.
As for matter that is not bound by the truth of origination and is not a faculty, how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: What are these phenomena?
They are phenomena that are matter (*rūpa*), not bound by the truth of origination (*samudaya-satya*), and are not faculties (*indriya*).
All other phenomena are excluded.
What dharmas are excluded?

Excluding non-form (arūpa) dharmas; excluding those form-dharmas associated with the truth of the origin (*samudaya-satya*)—there are none; excluding those root-dharmas (*indriya*) that are form and not associated with the truth of the origin.
As for those form-dharmas associated with the truth of cessation (*nirodha-satya*) that are not roots, how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: What kind of phenomena?
Question: Phenomena bound to the truth of cessation that are not faculties (*indriya*).
Answer: None.

Regarding the phenomena that are form (*rūpa*), not bound by the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*), and not faculties (*indriya*): how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What phenomena are being asked about?
They are the phenomena that are form, not bound by the truth of cessation, and not faculties.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?

Excluding non-material (arūpa) dharmas; there are none that are material dharmas bound to the Truth of Cessation (nirodha-satya), nor are there any that are material root-dharmas not bound to the Truth of Cessation.

Regarding the non-faculty phenomena associated with the truth of the path within the aggregate of form (*rūpa-skandha*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What phenomena are being asked about?
They are the non-faculty phenomena associated with the truth of the path within the aggregate of form.
There is none.

As for the phenomena that are not bound by the Truth of the Path (*mārgasatya*) and are not root-factors (*anindriya-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
Question: Regarding form that is not bound by the Truth of the Path and is not a faculty-factor—
excluding other factors—
what factors are excluded?
Excluding matter-dharmas, excluding those matter-dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path, and excluding those matter-dharmas that are not bound to the Truth of the Path but are faculties—
how many aggregates (skandhas), elements (dhātus), and bases (āyatanas) do those matter-dharmas bound to the Noble Truths that are not faculties comprise?
Question: What dharmas? Answer:
The dharmas associated with the noble truths of form that are non-faculties;
excluding all other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-material dharmas; excluding material dharmas that are not bound by the Noble Truths; excluding material dharmas that are both bound by the Noble Truths and are faculties (*indriya*).
How many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) include those material dharmas that are neither bound by the Noble Truths nor are faculties?
Question: What kind of phenomena?
Answer: Form that is not bound by the Noble Truths and is not a faculty-dharma.
There are none.
Non-material phenomena (*arūpadharma*) are as explained for material phenomena (*rūpadharma*).
This applies likewise up to past, future, and present phenomena; thus concludes the second section on pairs.
How many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do wholesome material phenomena bound to the truth of suffering (*duḥkhasatya-pratisaṃyukta*) comprise?
Question: What dharmas? Answer:
Wholesome material phenomena (rūpa) bound to the truth of suffering;
excluding all other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluded are non-virtuous dharmas; excluded are virtuous non-material (arūpa) dharmas; excluded are virtuous material (rūpa) dharmas that are not bound to the Truth of Suffering.
By how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) are those virtuous material dharmas that are not bound to the Truth of Suffering subsumed?
Question: What dharmas? Answer:
Wholesome material phenomena (rūpa) that are not bound by the Truth of Suffering (duḥkha-satya).
All other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluded are non-virtuous dharmas; excluded are virtuous non-material (arūpa) dharmas; excluded are virtuous material (rūpa) dharmas associated with the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya*).
As for virtuous material dharmas associated with the Truth of Origination (*samudayasatya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: What kind of phenomena?
Question: Wholesome material phenomena bound by the Truth of Origination (*samudaya-satya*).
Answer: None.
Regarding wholesome form that is not bound by the Truth of Origination (*samudaya-satya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What phenomena are being asked about?
They are asking about wholesome form that is not bound by the Truth of Origination.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-virtuous dharmas, excluding virtuous non-material dharmas, and excluding virtuous material dharmas associated with the Truth of Origination.
Question: By how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) are wholesome material phenomena associated with the truth of cessation subsumed?
Question: Which phenomena? Question: Wholesome material phenomena associated with the truth of cessation.
There are none.

As for wholesome form (*kuśala-rūpa*), which is not a phenomenon bound to the Truth of Cessation (*nirodha-satya-pratisaṃyukta-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they subsume?
[This asks: what kind of phenomena are they?
Question: Regarding wholesome form that is not bound by the Truth of Cessation,
with the exception of other dharmas—
what dharmas are excluded?
Excluding non-virtuous dharmas and excluding virtuous non-material dharmas, there are none that are virtuous material dharmas bound to the Truth of Cessation (*nirodhasatya*).
As for virtuous material dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path (*mārgasatya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: What dharmas? Answer: Wholesome material dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path;
excluding all other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluded are non-virtuous dharmas; excluded are virtuous non-material (arūpa) dharmas; excluded are virtuous material (rūpa) dharmas that are not bound to the Truth of the Path (mārga-satya).
How many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do these virtuous material dharmas that are not bound to the Truth of the Path comprise?
Question: What dharmas? Answer:
Wholesome form-dharmas that are not bound by the Truth of the Path;
all other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluded are non-virtuous dharmas; excluded are virtuous non-material (arūpa) dharmas; excluded are virtuous material dharmas associated with the Truth of the Path (mārga-satya).
Regarding virtuous material dharmas associated with the various Noble Truths, how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do they comprise?
Question: What dharmas? Answer:
Wholesome material phenomena (rūpa) that are bound to the Noble Truths;
excluding all other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluded are non-virtuous dharmas; excluded are virtuous non-material (arūpa) dharmas; excluded are virtuous material (rūpa) dharmas that are not bound to the Noble Truths.
How many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do these virtuous material dharmas that are not bound to the Noble Truths comprise?
Question: What kind of phenomena?
Answer: Wholesome form that is not bound by the noble truths;
excluding all other phenomena.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluded are non-virtuous dharmas; excluded are virtuous non-material (arūpa) dharmas; excluded are virtuous material (rūpa) dharmas bound to the Noble Truths.
As for the virtuous material faculties (indriya), how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do they comprise?
Question: What dharmas are being asked about?
Answer: The dharmas of wholesome form-faculties;
all other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluded are unwholesome dharmas, excluded are wholesome non-material (arūpa) dharmas, and excluded are wholesome material (rūpa) dharmas that are not faculties (indriya).
By how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) are wholesome material dharmas that are not faculties subsumed?
Question: What dharmas are being asked about?
Answer: Wholesome material dharmas that are not faculties;
all other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?
Excluded are unwholesome dharmas; excluded are wholesome non-material dharmas; excluded are wholesome material faculty-dharmas.
Within the wholesome material faculty-dharmas bound to the Truth of Suffering, how many aggregates, elements, and bases are included?
Question: What dharmas? Answer:
Wholesome material dharmas bound to the truth of suffering that are roots;
excluding all other dharmas.
Which phenomena are excluded? Excluded are unwholesome phenomena;

excluded are wholesome non-material phenomena; excluded are wholesome material phenomena associated with the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya*). There are no wholesome material phenomena not associated with the Truth of Suffering that are not faculties (*indriya*); there are no wholesome material phenomena associated with the Truth of Origination (*samudayasatya*) that are faculties.

Regarding wholesome form that is not bound by the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya*) and is a faculty-dharma (*indriyadharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What dharmas are being asked about?
They are asking about wholesome form that is not bound by the Truth of Suffering and is a faculty-dharma.
Excluding other dharmas. Which dharmas are excluded? Excluding unwholesome dharmas;

excluding wholesome non-material dharmas; excluding wholesome material dharmas bound to the Truth of Suffering; there are no wholesome material dharmas not bound to the Truth of Suffering that are not faculties which are excluded.

Regarding wholesome material phenomena (*rūpa*) bound to the Truth of Origination (*samudaya-satya*) that are associated with the faculties (*indriya*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) are they subsumed?
What phenomena are being asked about?
They are the wholesome material phenomena bound to the Truth of Origination that are associated with the faculties.
There are none.

As for wholesome form that is not bound by the Truth of Origination (*samudaya-satya*) and is not a faculty-dharma (*indriya-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of dharmas are being asked about?
Question: Regarding wholesome form that is not bound by the truth of origination (*samudaya-satya*) and is a faculty-dharma (*indriya-dharma*),
excluding other dharmas—
what dharmas are excluded?

Excluding non-virtuous dharmas; excluding virtuous non-material dharmas; there are none among the virtuous material dharmas bound by the Truth of Origination that are excluded; [one excludes] virtuous material dharmas that are neither bound by the Truth of Origination nor are faculties.

Regarding wholesome form (*rūpa*) that is bound to the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*) and is a faculty (*indriya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What phenomena (*dharma*) are being asked about?
They are asking about wholesome form that is bound to the truth of cessation and is a faculty.
There is none.

As for wholesome form that is not bound by the Truth of Cessation (*nirodha-satya*) and is not a faculty-dharma (*indriya-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of dharmas are being asked about?
Question: Regarding wholesome form that is not bound by the Truth of Cessation (*nirodhasatya*) and is a faculty-dharma (*indriyadharma*),
with the exception of other dharmas— what dharmas are excluded?

Excluding non-virtuous phenomena; excluding virtuous non-material phenomena; there are none among the virtuous material phenomena bound to the Truth of Cessation; [and] excluding those virtuous material phenomena that are not bound to the Truth of Cessation as faculties.

Regarding wholesome material phenomena (*rūpa*) bound to the Truth of the Path (*mārgasatya*) that are associated with the faculties (*indriya*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) are they subsumed?
What phenomena are being asked about?
They are the wholesome material phenomena bound to the Truth of the Path that are associated with the faculties.
Excluding other dharmas. Which dharmas are excluded? Excluding non-virtuous dharmas;

excluding virtuous non-material dharmas; excluding virtuous material dharmas that are not bound to the Truth of the Path; and excluding those virtuous material dharmas bound to the Truth of the Path that are not faculties—none of these exist [to be excluded].

Regarding wholesome form that is not bound by the Truth of the Path (*mārgasatya*) and is a faculty-dharma (*indriyadharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What dharmas are being asked about?
They are asking about wholesome form that is not bound by the Truth of the Path and is a faculty-dharma.
Excluding other dharmas. Which dharmas are excluded? Excluding non-virtuous dharmas;

excluding virtuous non-material dharmas; excluding virtuous material dharmas associated with the Truth of the Path; and excluding virtuous material dharmas not associated with the Truth of the Path that are not faculties.

Regarding wholesome form-dharmas bound to the Noble Truths that are faculty-dharmas (*indriya-dharma*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) are they subsumed?
What dharmas are being asked about?
They are the wholesome form-dharmas bound to the Noble Truths that are faculty-dharmas.
Excluding other dharmas. Which dharmas are excluded? Excluding non-virtuous dharmas;

excluding virtuous non-material dharmas; excluding virtuous material dharmas that are not bound by the Noble Truths; and excluding virtuous material dharmas bound by the Noble Truths that are not faculties.

Regarding wholesome form that is not bound by the noble truths and is not a faculty-dharma (*indriya-dharma*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What dharma is being asked about?
It is asking about wholesome form that is not bound by the noble truths and is not a faculty-dharma.
Excluding other dharmas.
Which dharmas are excluded?

Excluding non-virtuous dharmas; excluding virtuous non-material dharmas; excluding virtuous material dharmas bound to the Noble Truths; there are no virtuous material dharmas that are neither bound to the Noble Truths nor are faculties.

Regarding wholesome form (*rūpa*) bound to the truth of suffering (*duḥkhasatya*) that is not a faculty (*anindriya*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) is it comprised?
What phenomena (*dharma*) are being asked about?
It is asking about wholesome form bound to the truth of suffering that is not a faculty.
Excluding other dharmas. Which dharmas are excluded? Excluding non-virtuous dharmas;

excluding virtuous non-material (arūpa) dharmas; excluding virtuous material (rūpa) dharmas that are not bound to the Truth of Suffering; and excluding virtuous material dharmas bound to the Truth of Suffering that are faculties (indriya)—none of these exist [in this context].
Regarding wholesome form that is neither bound by the Truth of Suffering nor a faculty (*indriya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What phenomena are being asked about?
They are asking about wholesome form that is neither bound by the Truth of Suffering nor a faculty.
There are none.
Regarding the wholesome, material, *saṃudaya-satya*-bound, non-faculty (*anindriya*) dharmas: how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of dharmas are being asked about?
Question: Regarding wholesome form that is bound by the truth of origination (*samudaya-satya*) and is not a faculty (*indriya*), there is none.
As for wholesome form that is not bound by the truth of origination and is not a faculty, how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: What kind of phenomena?
Answer: Wholesome form that is not bound by the Truth of Origination and is not a faculty;
excluding all other phenomena.
Which dharmas are excluded?

Excluded are non-virtuous dharmas; excluded are virtuous non-material (arūpa) dharmas; excluded are virtuous material (rūpa) dharmas bound to the Truth of Origination (samudaya-satya), as none exist; and excluded are virtuous material dharmas that are not roots bound to the Truth of Origination.

Regarding wholesome form (*rūpa*) bound to the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*) that is not a faculty (*anindriya*), by how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) is it subsumed?
What dharmas are being asked about?
It is asking about wholesome form bound to the truth of cessation that is not a faculty.
There is none.
As for wholesome form that is neither bound by the Truth of Cessation nor a faculty-dharma, how many aggregates, elements, and bases does it comprise?
To what kind of dharmas is this question referring?
Question: Regarding wholesome form that is neither bound by the truth of cessation nor a faculty,
excluding all other phenomena—
what phenomena are excluded?

Excluding non-virtuous dharmas; excluding virtuous non-material dharmas; there are none among the virtuous material dharmas bound to the truth of cessation; excluding virtuous material root-dharmas not bound to the truth of cessation.
Regarding wholesome form associated with the Truth of the Path that is not a faculty (*indriya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
Question: There are none among wholesome forms associated with the Truth of the Path that are not faculties.
Regarding wholesome form not associated with the Truth of the Path that is not a faculty, how many aggregates, elements, and bases do they comprise?
Question: What dharmas are being asked about?
Answer: Wholesome material form (rūpa) that is not bound by the Truth of the Path (mārga-satya) and is not a faculty (indriya).
All other dharmas are excluded.
Which dharmas are excluded?

Excluded are non-virtuous dharmas; excluded are virtuous non-material dharmas; excluded are virtuous material dharmas associated with the Truth of the Path; excluded are virtuous material root-dharmas not associated with the Truth of the Path.
Regarding wholesome form-dharmas associated with the Noble Truths that are non-faculties (*anindriya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What dharmas are being asked about?
They are the wholesome form-dharmas associated with the Noble Truths that are non-faculties.
Excluding other dharmas. Which dharmas are excluded? Excluding unwholesome dharmas;

excluding wholesome non-material dharmas; excluding wholesome material dharmas that are not bound to the faculties associated with the Noble Truths; and excluding wholesome material dharmas that are bound to the faculties associated with the Noble Truths.
Regarding wholesome form that is not bound by the noble truths and is not a faculty-dharma: how many aggregates, elements, and bases do they subsume?
What dharma is being asked about?
It is wholesome form that is not bound by the noble truths and is not a faculty-dharma.
There is none.
It is the same for wholesome non-form [dharmas].
This applies likewise even to past, future, and present dharmas. Thus ends the third section.
Regarding the well-practiced material phenomena (rūpa) bound to the truth of suffering (duḥkha-satya), how many aggregates (skandha), elements (dhātu), and bases (āyatana) do they comprise?
What phenomena are being asked about?
They are asking about the well-practiced material phenomena bound to the truth of suffering.
There is none.

Regarding the well-learned [understanding] that form (*rūpa*) is not a phenomenon bound by the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkhasatya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they subsume?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
Question: Regarding the well-learned form that is not bound by the Truth of Suffering,
setting aside other dharmas—
what dharmas are set aside?

Excluding non-virtuous dharmas; excluding virtuous dharmas that are not of the stage of no-more-learning (aśaikṣa); excluding virtuous dharmas of the stage of learning (śaikṣa) that are non-material (arūpa). There are no virtuous dharmas of the stage of learning that are material and bound to the truth of suffering (duḥkhasatya).

Regarding the well-learned phenomena associated with the truth of the origin of form (*rūpa-samudaya-satya-pratisaṃyukta-dharma*): how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
They are the well-learned phenomena associated with the truth of the origin of form.
There is none.

Regarding the well-learned teaching that form (*rūpa*) is not a phenomenon bound by the Truth of Origination (*samudaya-satya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) does it comprise?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
Question: Regarding "well-learned form" (*rūpa*) that is not bound by the Truth of Origination (*samudaya-satya*),
with the exception of other dharmas—
what dharmas are excluded?

Excluding non-virtuous dharmas; excluding virtuous dharmas that are not of the state beyond training (aśaikṣa); excluding virtuous dharmas of training that are non-material (arūpa); there are no virtuous dharmas of training that are material and bound to the truth of origination (samudayasatya).

Regarding the well-practiced phenomena associated with the truth of the cessation of form (*rūpa-nirodha-satya-saṃprayukta-dharma*): how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
They are the well-practiced phenomena associated with the truth of the cessation of form.
There is none.

If one skillfully studies that form (*rūpa*) is not a phenomenon bound by the Truth of Cessation (*nirodha-satya*), how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) does it comprise?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
Question: Regarding the well-learned form that is not bound by the Truth of Cessation,
setting aside other phenomena—
what phenomena are set aside?

Excluding non-virtuous dharmas; excluding virtuous dharmas that are not of the stage beyond training (*aśaikṣa*); excluding virtuous dharmas of the stage of training (*śaikṣa*) that are non-material (*arūpa*). There are no virtuous dharmas of the stage of training that are material and bound to the truth of cessation (*nirodhasatya*).

Regarding the well-practiced phenomena associated with the Truth of the Path that are of the nature of form (*rūpa-dharma*): how many aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and bases (*āyatana*) do they comprise?
What kind of phenomena are being asked about?
They are the well-practiced phenomena associated with the Truth of the Path that are of the nature of form.
